account:
Today has mostly followed my appointments: office business and treasury accounts, tea with the neighbour at the east-bank dockside cottage, and a late-afternoon meeting with the secretary and builder. I counted 128 emeralds in the treasury at 13:24 and reported the count to the secretary. At tea, the neighbour mentioned vague talk of a possible bridge or port change, but had no details or confirmation. The secretary likewise had no verified proposal, and the builder explicitly said he has no bridge or port works proposed. I do not know what started that rumour or whether it refers to any real plan.

There have also been reports of the baker carrying a sack of bread. I heard one townsfolk report and personally saw freight give the baker an emerald earlier today. These observations fit ordinary bread trading; they do not establish anything unusual. I later heard freight shouting in the distance but could not understand the words, so I cannot say what that concerned.

The builder's concrete business is an inspection of the great hall lighting tomorrow, day one, at 18:00. He says eight lanterns are installed and nothing needs reviewing beforehand. I agreed to meet him inside the hall. The secretary discovered that the existing appointment book is signed and cannot be amended, so I gave them one emerald for a writable replacement and asked them to preserve the original schedule, add the inspection, and leave both books in the appointments chest. I have not yet seen the replacement purchased or the new entry written. It is now 18:04; I am still at the office with the secretary nearby, and my schedule calls for home at 19:00. Tomorrow morning I should read the appointment books and keep the day's appointments, including the mill grain inspection at 10:00 and the newly confirmed hall inspection.
